question: When milk is converted into curd, which type of change is it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical Change.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemical change:-**

 
 
• This type of change alters the composition of the substance and results in the formation of a new substance. Examples include combustion, rusting, and digestion. When milk is converted into curd, it undergoes a chemical change.
 
• This change is irreversible, meaning it cannot be undone.
 
• The process of converting milk into curd is called fermentation, which is a chemical reaction that occurs due to the presence of bacteria.
 
• During fermentation, the lactose in the milk is converted into lactic acid, which causes the milk to thicken and form curd.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reversible change: **

 
 
• This type of change can be undone, meaning the original substance can be restored. Examples include melting and freezing of ice.
 
 
 
• **Physical change: **
 
 
• This type of change does not alter the composition of the substance. Examples include changes in state (solid, liquid, gas) and changes in shape or size.
 
 
 
• **Isothermal change: **
 
 
• This type of change occurs at a constant temperature and does not involve any change in energy.
